blocks.text: DSPM identifies files and tables containing sensitive data and generates evidence data for review. You can configure an AWS S3 bucket or Azure storage account container to store these classified evidence data snippets. You can also use an existing storage account or S3 bucket present in one of the regions selected while onboarding or allow DSPM to create a new one in the orchestrator account.
The S3 bucket or storage account container cannot be changed after it is added. You can only enable or disable the evidence configuration.
The following flowchart details decision-making and configuration steps for evidence storage across AWS, Azure, and GCP, including both custom-managed and Zscaler-managed options.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Cloud Accounts.
Click Manage, and then select Manage Evidence.
On the Evidence Configuration page, click the toggle to enable or disable the evidence configuration.
When disabled, DSPM stops sending evidence data to the specified storage account.
Enter the existing S3 bucket details:
S3 Bucket Name: The name of the S3 bucket.
S3 Bucket Account ID: The 12-digit account ID of the S3 bucket.
KMS Key ARN: The KMS key or CMK key ARN. This key is used to encrypt the evidence data in the S3 bucket.
DSPM creates an S3 bucket in the orchestrator account to upload the evidence data.
Select the CloudFormation or Terraform template.
Download the template and run it on the account where the specified S3 bucket is present.
On the Apply Changes page, click Done.
To configure evidence storage for Azure, Zscaler recommends you to use the latest onboarding templates.
Enter the existing storage account details:
Storage Account Resource ID: The resource ID of the storage account.
Container Name: The name of the container.
Key Vault Resource ID: The resource ID of the key vault. This key vault is used to encrypt the evidence data in the container.
DSPM creates a storage container in the orchestrator account to upload the snippet of evidence data.
On the Apply Changes page, download the Evidence template and run it on the account where the storage account container is present.

For Zscaler Managed Container storage type, if you select Deploy private endpoint for secure communication while onboarding, you must add your system's IP address to the Azure key vault created in the orchestrator account before running the evidence template. This is required when multiple users need to apply Terraform from different IP addresses.
Sign in to the Azure portal and go to Key vaults.
On the Key vaults page, search and select the key vault created in the orchestrator account.
In the left-side navigation, go to Settings > Networking.
On the Firewalls and virtual networks tab:
Select Allow public access from specific virtual networks and IP addresses.
In the Firewall section, click Add your client IP address and enter your system's IP address.
On the Apply Changes page, click Done.
Enter the name of the bucket where you want to store the evidence data.
DSPM creates a bucket in the orchestrator project to upload the evidence data.
On the Apply Changes page, download the template and run it on the project where the specified bucket is present.
On the Apply Changes page, click Done.
